title: Songwriters in the Round
description: 1st & 3rd Wednesdays at ROOTED Cafe at 7 PM Four songwriters take the stage, seated in a comfortable semi-circle. They take turns playing songs, occasionally joining in with each other on harmony vocals or guitar licks. The format encourages conversation between the writers, which gives the audience an opportunity to hear these creative people talk as if in their own living rooms. Inspired by the “guitar pulls” of the legendary Bluebird Café in Nashville. You might hear a young up-and-coming pro, an established mid-career performer and mentor, and a cherished elder of the scene — all sharing music. The growing relationships will warm your heart and enrich your soul. Come every week as the lineup shifts and new friends are made.

title: Harrison Goodell
description: Harrison Goodell – Tough Love Tour One of the Northeast’s top emerging artists, Harrison Goodell brings his full band to The Rockwell for a night of indie folk and Americana. His music lives somewhere between intimate storytelling and full-band energy that fills a room. Instagram/facebook @ harrisongoodell Harrison Goodell is a singer-songwriter from Seacoast New Hampshire, weaving indie-folk songs that feel like home – restless, familiar, and always shifting.His sound, while uniquely his own, sits between anthemic folk and confessional songwriting, earning comparisons to artists like Noah Kahan and The Lumineers. Harrison ’s dedication to his craft has led to sold-out shows and opening slots for artists like Sara Bareilles, JP Saxe and The Lone Bellow. His music has been championed by tastemaker Ari Elkins, whose 2.2 million followers have helped bring Harrison ’s unvarnished storytelling to a wider audience. As one of the Northeast’s top emerging artists, he was awarded a grant from The Portsmouth Music Hall, further fueling his rise. With new material on the way and sessions in Nashville with some of the industry’s most exciting writers, 2026 is set to be a defining year. title: bellwire
description: bellwire SHOW DESCRIPTION: bellwire return to Boston with a new song in their bittersweet register tackling love, existence, and entropy. “LOVEBIRDS” (featuring a fellow sweet prince of New England songcraft, Jake McKelvie, singing harmony). The song will come out on the morning of the show. Since frontman Tyler berd’s move to the west coast, the full bellwire is at most a twice-a-year sighting in these haunts. Don’t sleep on this, especially with their roadworn pirate pedal-steel player Jonee Earthquake at the slide and pedals. They will be joined by two local favorites: Yes, Chef and Mel Starr and the Astral Projection. ARTIST BIOS: bellwire is a New England rock band first formed in the summer of 2011, now most commonly spotted in the fall. Early experiments in lo-fi, surf, and punk gave way to their jangly power-pop style typified on the EP, Dog Thoughts . Their self-titled 2022 LP is an alt-country concept album that tells a story of love and loss (single: Dreamin’ ). Often appearing with New England pirate-punk stalwart Jonee Earthquake on pedal steel, their high-energy performances still put lyrics and story first. Their songs use clowns, birds, weather, and magically mundane (or maybe just random?) images to convey emotional experiences. They reflect on family, grief, relationships and finding oneself in their writing. Mel cares deeply about mental health and community wellbeing, using music as a path to bring people together in learning and collaboration. title: Hippies & Cowboys w Velvet Daydream
description: Hippies & Cowboys with Velvet Daydream Hippies And Cowboys are a powerhouse rock ’n’ soul band out of Nashville, TN, built on grit, groove, and the raw electricity of classic Southern rock—revived with a modern edge. Their sound fuses deep-pocket soul, blues, and rock ’n’ roll, channeling icons such as Aerosmith, The Allman Brothers, Tedeschi Trucks and others. Rooted in tradition and sharpened by the road, Hippies And Cowboys cut their early recordings in legendary rooms including FAME Studios, Muscle Shoals Sound, and East Avalon—capturing the same spirit that shaped generations of American music. Their debut release, Live at Fox and Locke (2023), bottled the raw, no-holds-barred energy of their live show and quickly earned critical acclaim. The follow-up EP, Fork in the Road (2024), doubled down with a gritty, hard-hitting collection of songs that showcased their deep Southern roots, tight musicianship, and fearless songwriting. A live double album and full concert film are slated for release in 2026. title: Abby Holliday, Charli Adams
description: Abby Holliday + Charli Adams There comes a time in every artist’s career when the art form transcends a mere outlet for self-expression and becomes a universal gift to mankind. For some it takes years, for Abby Holliday it was there from the start. Her vulnerable introspection and brutal lyricism combined with mind-bending sonic sensibilities and a distinct production style immediately fused a bond between her and her loyal fan base. Holliday masterfully guides listeners through moments in time extremely specific to her own life that puts words to collective experiences of the human condition, reaching into places we might not have known existed prior. Abby found her voice during her early years of college where she began quietly writing songs in the confines of her room. After a friend heard the songs and encouraged her to share them, Abby met producer Jonathan Class and set off to record her debut album WHEN WE’RE FAR APART I FALL APART. It was in these studio moments where Abby’s sound began to take shape, a launchpad for her sophomore album I’M OK NO I’M NOT. Holliday and Class experiment with a wide range of sounds from vocoded vocal stacks, to jarring synths, to lush strings and piano, to a tasteful blend of organic and synthetic rhythm sections amassing in a discography that runs the gambit of the most beautiful songs to songs that smack you in the face with unforgettable hooks and driving beats. CRACK A SMILE COME ON STAY A WHILE, Holliday’s highly anticipated junior record, is out now. “Former cheer captain” isn’t something you always see on the resume of a rising, alternative singer-songwriter. For Charli Adams, who grew up across several small towns in rural Alabama, an outward display of optimism might have been the only way to get by. title: Lucky Gold Jr. & Werewolf
description: Lucky Gold Jr. & Werewolf SHOW DESCRIPTION: Two East-Coast-via-Ohio based indie projects will be rocking the Rockwell on August 11th with support from a secret special guest! ARTIST BIOS: Lucky Gold Jr. is a folk-rock project led by Massachusetts-based singer-songwriter Ellie Fallon, with frequent live and recorded support from her sibling Mimi Fallon on bass, and producer, instrumentalist, & friend Ollie Peterson. Fallon has anchored her sound to nostalgia’s ephemera, unraveling unique experiences with familiar language. She writes about everything from failure to fandom with a perspective informed by hope, and a sound inspired by her collaborators and musical fixations alike. Oliver Peterson, under the name Werewolf, records alone from his carpet-padded garage in Stamford, Connecticut. Through one-wire systems, meticulously-crafted ambient textures, and natural melodic sensibilities, Peterson produces a sophisticated sound that ascends the parts of its sum, and escapes time and place while kneeling in worship to it. Werewolf marries the grounded – acoustic guitars, crunchy drums, raw vocals – with the ethereal – swirling drones, surreally visceral lyricism, abstract visual components – to build a dream pop, shoegaze, indie-rock vision that is entirely his own. title: The Darkness Behind
description: The Darkness Behind SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Darkness Behind is a solo multimedia performance that explores the many meanings behind the title: surviving darkness, leaving darkness behind, and the ongoing tension between memory and freedom. Ameen’s musical journey during the ISIS occupation of his hometown in Iraq, Mosul, 2014-2017, and the musical chapters post that period. Using violin, voice, live looping, and electronic textures, the performance combines cinematic music, experimental sound, and personal storytelling that creates an immersive live experience. This work follows performances at venues including The Metropolitan Museum of Art and One World Trade Center. ARTIST BIO: Award-winning Iraqi composer, performer, and multidisciplinary artist, born In Baghdad 1989. Ameen’s work across film, theater, and contemporary music, and he is internationally active collaborator with ensembles and institutions in the U.S., Middle, East, and Europe. title: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt
description: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Scene Within the Scene is a local community building platform for artists and musicians to connect and support one another. This is the first show curated by this group which is completely non profit. The bands on this first show are High Energy Rock bands with influences from Garage/Surf Punk/ and Psych Rock. ARTIST BIOS: Kooked Out: “The kaleidoscopic sound of Kooked Out has evolved naturally throughout the years and draws influences from almost every genre and decade of music from the 1930s to present day, crafting a unique mix of styles and sounds that have developed Kooked Out a cult-like following in the skate and surf communities. Leaning heavily into the music of the ’50s, ’60s and early 2000s, Kooked Out’s genre-spanning sound has become a calling card, both on record and live on stage, appropriate for a creative outlet that lists its top influences as The White Stripes, The Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, Dick Dale, The Black Keys, Cage The Elephant, and Blink-182.” -Michael Marotta / Knyvet Members: John Fiore, Chris Laskey, Chris Caduto, Emily Trubey / ‘2024 Live Act Of The Year’ New England Music Awards Viper Cut Eyes: Boston’s unapologetically noisy and transcendent Surfadelic Psych Rock unit Ace McGuire’s Acid Tabs are defibrillating stagnant bodies with blood pulsing riffs paired with a hit of tape echoed and verbed out psychedelia. Originally a bedroom recording project of Bermudian singer and songwriter Liv Dunks and New Bedford MA’s guitarist, singer and producer Mitch Cardoza, they expanded their vision by adding San Francisco’s multi-instrumentalist Erik Dietz on bass. Stunt!: Brings the attitude and aggression of 90s Rock bands to today’s pop music scene. Riffs inspired by the grunge and pop-punk sounds of yesterday meld with vocal melodies that hang with any of today’s radio ear worms. title: EVERFINER Shimmer Funk Cosmic Gala
description: EVERFINER Shimmer Funk Cosmic Gala SHOW DESCRIPTION: Join EVERFINER in a cosmic shimmer celebration of music as the group conjures its 2nd EP, Shimmer Funk, from the depths of Nova 37 in EFNR Star Belt. You may find yourself unable to stop dancing to these tunes, but fear not. Shimmer Funk has been crafted over the past year with the magical properties required to get your body moving and grooving. Resume your position on the bridge, strap into the cockpit of your star vessel, and prepare for a shimmer space journey. ARTIST BIOS: EVERFINER is a Boston based six-piece ensemble rocking thoughtful originals in overlapping genres including, shimmer-folk, shimmer-funk, soul, and pop. BIG HUGE harmonies lay on top of a tight, minimalist rhythm section, and if you’re lucky a horn section will casually be lowered from the rafters. Lyrically, these tunes work through issues of identity, boundaries, long distance relationships, short distance situationships, and the flux of family. The band is a beautiful collective of musicians who care as much about each other as they do about their art. As we all grow and learn, each day we are all becoming a little more EVERFINER. Their self-described sound “grit-pop” weaves the the nerve of post-grunge, brightness of power pop, & the introspection of 90s alt-rock. Jac Mestel’s unfiltered, heart-on-sleeve lyrics entwine with catchy-AF melodies and emerge as vocals that have been known to turn heads. Derek Bergstrom’s creamy bass counter-melodies mix with Mestel’s driving guitar. Jess Townsend’s (World/Inferno) unique, expressive drumming is the underlying pulse that brings the band to life. title: Nelward
description: Nelward nelward is an innovative music artist creating funky electronic artpop for the internet age. Early on, the melodies of classic Nintendo games were etched into his ADHD brain and never seemed to leave. Drawing from a wide array of influences, nelward enjoys the explorative aspect of music creation and is not one to dwell in one sound for too long. He is also known for the colorful and whimsical art direction in his often self-produced videos. In 2017, his first EP Alive in Screen established his foundational sound. The subsequent success of the new jack swing/nu metal banger Ghost / Getting Better and bubblegum pop earworm Never Wanna Fall in Love With U established him as a force to be reckoned with in the independent electronic music scene. 2020’s Eat Your Dreams EP delved into heavier subject matter while tightening nelward’s knack for catchy songwriting. 2024’s single THE RUNAROUND combines infectious earworms while embracing musical exploration. Nelward is known for his animated live performances, completing a 40+ date tour of North America and Europe with TWRP from 2024-2025. In 2025 the nelward live band was born, representing a distinct chapter in the evolution of his live performance. Nelward represents a growing segment of independent electronic artists who are building significant followings through digital platforms while creating innovative multimedia art experiences. Justice Cow is the cosmic gumbo of Jessica Kion. She grew up in a musical family which meant pressing rewind until she had transcribed every word of the “Grease” soundtrack and being forced to sing barbershop quartet family-style in the car. For over a decade she has toured extensively across the US and abroad, equally at home in living rooms, rock clubs, and festival stages. title: Mr. Phylzzz and friends
description: Mr. Phylzzz and friends Chicago spreads their net of sonic oddities throughout our great nation as two piece noise rockers Mr.Phylzzz (Amphetamine Reptile Records) returns to the road. Hot off of their tour with Melvins and Boris, Mr.P is going to summon up the spirits of fellow two-piece trash dogs BEDTIMEMAGIC, the wall-to-wall hedonism of Providence’s Magic Thinking Ape! Fans of stylized band names will be most pleased. ARTIST BIOS: •Mr.Phylzzz Formed in 2015 by founding member Clinton Jacob as a joke. Mr.Phylzzz (pronounced Flyzzz) is an ever changing monster of noise. Over time Mr.Phylzzz has formed a heavy wall of sound filled with hooky riffs and melodic vocals- creating a chaotic storm that’s well worth the painful wall of cranked amps and exploding drums. During the growing years, Phylzzz was doing small tours which landed them getting picked up in 2019 by Amphetamine Reptile Records (AmRep) to be featured in the legendary “Dope Guns ‘N Fucking in the Streets” Vol 14 comp. Later that year they released their debut album “Penitent Curtis” (2019), followed by “Cancel Culture Club” (2022) on AmRep. In 2023 the band released “Fat Chance” on Amrep and completed a full US tour supporting The Melvins and Boris. The band is Chicago based. Mr.Phylzzz is comprised of Clinton Jacobs (guitar/vox) & Danny Sein (drums). •BEDTIMEMAGIC Spicy as a very spicy thing, BEDTIMEMAGIC is a two-dog trash rock band from Boston, MA. They formed in 2013. They have at least three records out. Morgan Berns plays drums, foot organ, and does vocals. Nicholas Pentabona also does vocals, and he plays a bass that Morgan made. It’s really loud. They really think they are dogs. It’s a thing. •Magic Thinking Ape Nobody thinks MTA is smelly. Nobody. If you think that, you’re really mean. I don’t think I would want to be your friend if you think that. title: The Schizophonics
description: The Schizophonics Amps screaming. No exit in sight. The Schizophonics kick the door in and never let it close. This San Diego–based three-piece delivers a live show that’s loud and dangerously fun—an all-gas, no-brakes blast of feedback and groove. It’s full-contact rock ’n’ roll: high voltage, high velocity, and sharpened to a blade. The band features Pat Beers on vocals and guitar, Lety Beers on drums, and Sarah Linton on bass. Together they unleash a fuzz-soaked, funk-fueled attack built on pounding rhythm and feral energy. Every song hits like a charge. Every set feels like the floor might give out. Blink and you miss something. Stand still and you get run over. Forged on the road and fueled by motion, The Schizophonics have torn through stages in fourteen countries, earning a reputation as a must-see live act that turns rooms upside down. Channeling the raw spirit of James Brown, Iggy Pop, Jimi Hendrix, Little Richard, and The Sonics, they strip rock back to its most dangerous elements—and set them loose. — Schizophonics Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: This show is all ages. title: Julia Minkin
description: Julia Minkin SHOW DESCRIPTION: Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin is joined by Boston favorites Bowling Shoes and Cate Yoder for an evening of inventive indie music, compelling storytelling, and rich, genre-bending sounds. From shimmering synth-pop and art-rock experimentation to intimate folk melodies, this lineup offers music that’s as intelligent as it is fun. ARTIST BIOS: Julia Minken: Best known for co-writing viral hit songs with French electropop sensation Kid Francescoli, Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin steps into her own with her debut album Not Ready, co-created and produced with her husband Andrew Sudhibhasilp. Blending warm, folk-tinged vocals with nostalgic dance-floor energy and introspection, Minkin “finds her own creative voice, shimmering, rhythmic, and heartfelt—both bold and refreshingly sincere” (Thoughts Words Actions). Bowling Shoes: Melding innovative art-pop experimentalism with indie-rock nuance and arena-ready hooks, Boston, MA’s Bowling Shoes craft eminently catchy music sprinkled with delightful touches of subversive noise Cate Yoder: A double and electric bassist and guitarist from Richmond, Virginia, Cate Yoder learns about her environment through exploring, inventing, and performing a multitude of genres or really any music she can get hands on. Since being established primarily as a bass player, she is diving into the songwriting indie folk role with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. With airy melodies, detailed guitar, piano, and percussive elements, and bitter lyrics, she hopes to share her experience of finding solace and comfort in a complex world. ARTIST INSTAGRAMS: @ julia_minkin / @ bowlingshooz / @ cate_on_bass DOORS: 7:00 PM SHOW: 8:00 PM Age Limit: This event is All Ages ID: Valid ID required for alcohol consumption Limited Late Seating: Due to the architecture of our space, the entrance is next to the stage and it is disruptive to the performer to enter late. We will seat you

title: GHOSTWOMAN
description: GHOSTWOMAN GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. The music has always been beautifully inhospitable, earned only by those curious enough to seek it out. — Dine Alone Records Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: Show age differs by the day. Shows are All Ages Sundays-Thursdays & 21+ Fridays and Saturdays Valid ID required for Entry on Fridays & Saturdays Doors 7:00 PM Show 8:00 PM Refund Policy: REFUNDS DETERMINED BY GET TO THE GIG ADA Accessibility: The Rockwell is partially ADA Accessible with an elevator and restrooms in saloon wide enough for wheelchair use.

title: ☀️ Summer Series: Global Pulse
description: In honor of FIFA’s World Cup, Global Pulse is a diasporic celebration bringing together Haitian and Ghanaian performers including Dzidzor and Afmohip for an evening of music, rhythm, and cultural exchange.

title: Afmohip: Traveling Village
description: Under the direction of Mrs. JoJo Caidor, Afmohip proudly presents our first-ever full evening-length show, Traveling Village. A work rooted in the past, present, community, and connections.Traveling Village is a sequel that represents communities from different ethnic groups, paving the way and creating connections between the past and the present. It shows the beginnings of shared resources and mutual support, leading to the collective power found in solidarity. The strength of a single, shared force brings unison, togetherness, and courage. It acknowledges that struggles existed before and continue today, while reminding us of the reasons behind our current way of life. At its core, it emphasizes the importance of receiving, understanding, and sharing, allowing communities to endure and grow.

title: ☀️ Summer Series: Samba & Latin Dance Party
description: A high-energy night of live music and dance rooted in Latin and Brazilian traditions featuring Receita de Samba & Friends. This festive evening invites audiences to move, celebrate, and experience the rhythms that connect cultures across the Americas.

title: ☀️ Summer Series: The Summer Throwdown
description: The Summer Series concludes with The Summer Throwdown, MC’ed by the legendary Megatron, a high-energy end-of-season celebration featuring DJs, live performances, and an electrifying dance battle. This event brings the community together one final time to close out the summer with music and movement.

title: Yarumi González: Artist in Residence Showcase
description: The Artist in Residence Showcase celebrates the culmination of MAC’s residency program, highlighting works developed through sustained artistic exploration and experimentation. Rather than focusing solely on finished pieces, the showcase invites audiences into the creative process, offering a glimpse into evolving ideas and artistic discovery. MAC is honored to announce this year’s Artist in Residence, Yarumi González. During her residency, González will continue developing a multidisciplinary, autobiographical work exploring identity, migration, and the American Dream through poetic and ritual-inspired storytelling, movement, video, photography, installation, and performance.

title: Lift Every Voice: BIPOC Play Festival
description: A signature MAC program, Lift Every Voice amplifies the work of BIPOC playwrights, poets, and spoken word artists through staged readings and performances. The festival creates space for artists to share new work while fostering meaningful dialogue between creators and audiences.

title: Día de los Muertos Celebration
description: Honoring the rich Mexican tradition of Día de los Muertos, this immersive community celebration features music, dance, storytelling, and altar installations that invite audiences to reflect on ancestry, remembrance, and the enduring bonds between generations.

title: Barbed Wire
description: Each year we celebrate MLK – the person and the weekend – with a performance focused on the legacy of Black America from Civil Rights to today. This year we bring to the stage Barbed Wire, a new work presented in full for the first time on our stage.

title: The Fabric of Us: A Celebration of Black Fashion Through the Decades
description: This annual showcase celebrates the evolution of Black style, identity, and cultural expression across generations. Through original designs inspired by movements ranging from the Harlem Renaissance to contemporary fashion culture, the event highlights the lasting influence of Black creativity and innovation.

title: MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival
description: A new addition to MAC’s programming, MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival is a multi-day celebration of contemporary dance and movement-based performance. Bringing together choreographers, performers, and audiences, the festival creates opportunities for artistic experimentation, collaboration, and dialogue while expanding MAC’s presence within the dance community.Across the season, MAC continues to deepen its investment in artist development, signature cultural programming, and community-centered experiences that position the organization as both a creative incubator and a gathering place for diverse communities.Each performance will include the works of two dance companies, followed by a Q+A with one company.Tickets to individual performances are $40Choose tickets to any two performances, and receive 25% off your order!Choose tickets to all four performances, and receive 50% off your order!

title: Donizetti’s Lucia di Lammermoor
description: Join us for an unforgettable evening of gorgeous music, bel canto singing, and heartrending drama as Pico Opera presents Donizetti’s beloved tragedy, Lucia di Lammermoor.This intimate, fully staged production will be performed in Italian with English titles, accompanied by Pianist Aditya Raguram and our Pico Orchestra, directed by Daniel Pooley. All seats will be within 8 rows of the stage on stadium seating, ensuring a fully immersive and truly unique opera experience. Don’t miss out on this opportunity to experience the magic of opera up close and personal!

title: Cambridge Public Library Book Club
description: Every other month, we team up with the Cambridge Public Library to highlight contemporary works from marginalized voices. All over a fresh, craft beer, of course! For May, we plan on reading Death of the Soccer God by Dimitry Elias Leger - a passionate and improbable love story, and a roaring Pan-American tale about the price of fame. We’ll gather in person in our Broadway location’s back taproom on Wednesday, July 1st, at 7:00 pm for our monthly discussion. Grab a beer, cold brew, or kombucha at the front bar, then come find us in the back. The discussion is casual, and all are welcome – even if you don’t finish the book, we’d still love to have you. Copies of the book are available at the Main Library in Cambridge, at 449 Broadway. The e-book and digital audiobook can be borrowed through the Libby app. Let us know if you need help accessing the book. Please note that our taprooms are 21+ and all guests should be prepared to show a valid, current government-issued photo ID at the door. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Pepita Lo-Fi Friday
description: Lo-Fi Fridays are here! Just like our Lo-Fi weekends but now during the work week! Stop by the “secret” back taproom of our sweet little cafe space every Friday morning for a quiet sanctuary of productivity and peace. Need a bit of quiet time? The Lamplighter + Pepita team are here to bring you a little slice of calm. From here on out, we will open the back taproom from 8am-2pm on Friday mornings for Lo Fi Fridays. Think of it as a designated calming, quiet zone just for our Pepita patrons. We’ll play chill, ambient music to set the vibe, and folks are encouraged to read, work, study, etc. with minimal talking preferred. Grab a coffee and cozy up in the back taproom at our 284 Broadway location to soak up that tranquil energy or to get a jump start on the week ahead. Your weekend brunch plans have never been more relaxing! P.S. If you’re not feeling quiet time, the front taproom will remain open as usual for normal operations.

title: Brewery Yoga
description: Buy your tickets on Eventbrite! Looking for some healthy weekend plans? Join us for a Sunday morning brewery yoga class at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s Cambridge Crossing (CX) taproom. We’ll gather in the light-filled upstairs taproom for a gentle flow. Space is limited, and reservations are required. Save your spot through Eventbrite here! All yoga levels are welcome! This class is great for beginners, as well as for experienced yogis. We’ll lead you through a guided flow with a focus on stretching, breathing, and light activity – you might work up a light sweat, but nothing too strenuous. Please plan on bringing your own yoga mat. If you don’t have a mat, a large beach towel works as well. The class takes place in our upstairs taproom at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s CX location (110 N First St, Cambridge MA). Your ticket includes full access to the yoga class as well as a beer, cold brew coffee, or kombucha. Parking: There is street parking available, or the parking garage is available for $10 with Lamplighter validation. Show your ticket to a bartender before or after class to validate! This event is 21+ and all guests must show a valid government-issued ID. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com.

title: Broadway Trivia
description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! The game will start at 7:30 pm, and is about two hours long (with plenty of beer breaks, of course). Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Brewery Tour & Tasting
description: Break out your notebook and freshly sharpened No. 2 pencils because we’re going back to school! We're offering brewery tours at our original 284 Broadway location on the first Saturday of every month. Space is limited, so snag your spot right here by purchasing a ticket. Our knowledgeable team will lead you on an interactive, behind-the-scenes tour of the production floor at Lamp, where you’ll learn the essentials of craft beer-making, and how it all works at our compact, Cambridge-based facility. You'll also taste your way through the brewing process, sampling three of our current favorite draft pour picks, plus a special bonus beer to start the sipping syllabus. Will you graduate top of your class? Either way, we think you’ll find your new favorite subject. Each ticket includes: 🍻One 6 oz welcome beer, plus 3 - 5 oz flight glass-sized samples 🚶🏼A 60 min guided tasting and behind-the-scenes brewery tour 📝 Beer School "quiz" and informational answer key 📚 A Lamplighter Beer School diploma :) Questions? Get in touch! events@lamplighterbrewing.com. Please note that this event is 21+ and all guests will be asked to show a valid government-issued ID. Refund Policy We understand that plans sometimes change. If you provide us with more than 24 hours' notice prior to the event start time, we will issue a full refund to your original payment method. Within 24 hours of the start time, we will offer a refund in the form of credit to be used for a future ticketed event hosted by Lamplighter, valid for 1 year. Please note that Eventbrite fees, including processing and service fees, are nonrefundable as they are charged by Eventbrite and not under the control of Lamplighter. Please request refunds through Eventbrite, on your order confirmation page.

title: TCS presents: Demetrius Fields
description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.Demetrius Fields is a half-black, half-Lebanese comic born in Windsor, Ontario, and raised in the suburbs of Detroit, Michigan. He has made a name for himself in New York City, where he can be seen performing regularly at the New York Comedy Club and has been featured in the New York Comedy Festival. title: Worship: A Faith of Inclusion
description: As we listened to our leaders describe a war of choice as a "holy war", we witnessed a version of Christianity known as "Christian Nationalism", where anyone who disagrees is considered an enemy and a traitor. What is it that separates us, with our own Christian heritage, from the rage-filled rhetoric of this extremist ideology? Historically, Unitarian Universalists have upheld values of radical welcome and love for all of our neighbors, working to end the oppression of immigrants, the poor, and the disenfranchised; values we believed were enshrined in our constitution 250 years ago. As a "faith of inclusion", how do we reach toward others of faith, whose values seem very different from our own? Rev. Lisa Perry-Wood is preaching. Rev. Lisa Perry-Wood has had many professional careers over the years, working as a public librarian, a mental health administrator, charter school founder and principal, and in several nonprofit leadership roles. After attending seminary at Andover Newton, Lisa served several congregations: as ministerial intern at FRS in Carlisle, summer minister in Lexington and Winchester, parish minister in Bedford, settled senior minister at First Parish in Brookline, and, most recently, Interim Minister at First Parish in Wayland. She also spent two years working as a hospice chaplain. Rev. Lisa is a certified yoga teacher, with a certificate in Ayurvedic medicine. She identifies as a Buddhist-Mystic, practicing meditation and mindfulness, both on and off the cushion. She also loves walks in nature, swimming in the ocean or at Walden Pond, and playing with her grandchildren.

title: Worship: The Wisdom of Family Restaurants
description: The Wisdom of Family Restaurants Grilled Cheese! Sundaes! Being Yourself! What can we learn from Friendly’s, and other family restaurants, as multigenerational spaces? Join Rev. Stevie–Minister of Religious Education in Arlington, MA–to explore what it means to be a community of practice. Rev. Stevie remembers fondly serving First Parish Cambridge as our Summer Student Minister in 2016, and is glad to return to share this message. Rev. Stevie Carmody is preaching. Stevie came to Unitarian Universalism through First Parish Arlington, drawn in by how our community values young people. Regularly attending during high school, Stevie found a spiritual home here, and first felt a pull towards ministry. Stevie studied religion while attending Deep Springs College and Brown University. In his early twenties, Stevie worked in a preschool for children with autism in Providence, RI. During this time, Stevie also co-created a young adult social justice retreat at Rowe Camp & Conference Center. Stevie initially worked as First Parish’s Religious Education Assistant in 2014, under the direction of Tina Schultz. Called to UU ministry, Stevie completed a Master of Divinity program at Harvard Divinity School while simultaneously putting his ministry training into practice as the First Parish Youth Program Coordinator. Additionally, Stevie served as an intern minister at the First Unitarian Universalist Church of San Diego, CA. In 2019, First Parish voted to ordain Stevie, which we celebrated together in October of that year.

title: Art Study Center Seminar: Jacques de Gheyn II
description: This talk follows the remarkable career of Jacques de Gheyn II, a Flemish-born draughtsman and printmaker who arrived in the Northern Netherlands in the 1590s as part of a broader wave of artists fleeing war and upheaval in the south. Looking at prints and drawings in the Art Study Center, we will explore what it took for artists to reinvent themselves in one of Europe’s most dynamic and rapidly changing art markets. Led by: Susanne Bartels, Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Curatorial Fellow, Division of European and American Art

title: Summer Spotlight Tour
description: Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours of the collections. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram at @harvardarthappens.

title: New on View: Got Milk?
description: The Dutch Republic was one of Europe’s leading dairy producers in the 17th century, owing to its pastures and drained polders. Grazing herds yielded vast quantities of milk, butter, and cheese, which were exported across the continent and consumed at nearly every meal. Join curatorial fellow Susanne Bartels for a talk about the importance of dairy production in 17th-century Dutch society and how it is reflected in the artworks and literature of the time. This gallery talk is part of our New on View series, highlighting recent gallery installations and presenting new insights into recent acquisitions or old favorites. Led by: Susanne Bartels, Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Curatorial Fellow, Division of European and American Art

title: Gallery Performance: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: In celebration of the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages, Harvard student Samuel Puopolo will share some of his favorite Welsh medieval poetry, both in the original language and translated into English. Focusing on themes of resilience in the face of widespread change, these poems highlight the enduring cultural continuities of the Welsh as well as their deep-rooted commitment to poetry and song. Speaker: Samuel Puopolo, Ph.D. candidate in Celtic Languages and Literatures, Harvard University In Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026), discover the many forms of Celtic creativity and their artistic legacies in this sweeping story that spans ancient to modern times.

title: Art + Science: Cotton Duck Canvas
description: This event does not require registration; see further details below. Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join a member of our Straus Center staff for an informal conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, associate paintings conservator href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/about/staff/284">Ellen Davis will talk about the use of cotton duck canvas. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections. Space is limited, and this program is available on a first-come, first-served basis; no registration is required. The Harvard Art Museums offer href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">free admission every day, Tuesday through Sunday. Please see the href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/general-policies">museum visit page to learn about our general policies for visiting the museums.

title: Gray Area: Compassion and Companionship
description: The 14th-century tale of Saint Roch (Rocco) and his canine companion recounts the pair’s selfless compassion and care for those suffering. Join us to explore how today, amid global challenges such as pandemics and social isolation, the story serves as a reminder of the importance of humanitarian values and solidarity. This talk is part of Gray Area, a series that features members of our staff exploring artworks that capture the complexities of humanity, political landscapes, ethics, ideologies, power dynamics, and critical thinking in our times. Through this series, we hope to encourage people to observe and consider their own individual gray areas, and to think about how their unique experiences guide the choices they make. Led by: Jeanne Burke, Academic and Public Programs Coordinator, Division of Academic and Public Programs

title: Museum Class: Seeing Art with Matisse
description: Explore art history through the perspective of Henri Matisse in this four-week class that takes place in the galleries. With an emphasis on close looking and conversation, Matisse scholar Camran Mani will bring you inside the story of how art history delighted, inspired, and challenged this modern artist, and what he thought about topics from ancient sculpture and Islamic art to Cézanne and beyond. The museum was a space of a creative adventure for Matisse—this class aims to make it something similar for you. The class will be held every Thursday from September 10 to October 1.

title: Lectures On Tap: Cinematic Storytelling: Visual Structure in Film
description: Lectures On Tap: Cinematic Storytelling: Visual Structure in Film Event Description: Join us for an engaging evening as Prof. Drew McClellan unpacks how filmmakers communicate thoughts, emotions, and ideas through visual strategy and cinematic design. You’ll discover how every shot is carefully constructed to guide your emotions, deepen storytelling, and choreograph the eye across the frame. Through close analysis of still images and iconic scenes from classic and contemporary cinema, this lecture reveals the “secret” visual language used by directors, cinematographers, production designers, and editors to shape and enhance the audience experience. Whether you’re a filmmaker, film lover, designer, student, or simply curious about why movies “feel” the way they do, this session offers an accessible and inspiring look at the architecture of cinematic storytelling—and will forever change the way you watch films. Drew McClellan is an award-winning educator, filmmaker, and visual strategist whose work focuses on the intersection of cinematic storytelling and visual strategy. He serves as an adjunct professor at the USC School of Cinematic Arts and is currently Chair of the Cinematic Arts Department at the Los Angeles County High School for the Arts (LACHSA). description: Character Creation For anyone who gets excited performing as someone else, this is the class for you! For anyone who wants to get more comfortable performing as someone else, this class is for you! For 6 weeks we will explore different characters and how they propel stories and shows forward! DATES: June 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, July 6 (showcase) TIME: Check-in: 5:45pm Class: 6pm-9pm COST: $300 / $350/ $400 for 6 classes, 3 hours each *Returning students are eligible for 20% off ($260 use code RETURNINGCLOWN) **Two work trade/skill share scholarships are available for new students. Email deby@therockwell.org to apply. MEET DEBY! Deby Xiadani is the Artistic Director of The Rockwell, as well as a director, comedian, writer, actor, and devisor passionate about creating bold new work. With a love for physical comedy rooted in a childhood obsession with Jim Carrey, Deby has developed a unique voice that blends playfulness, heart, and fearless experimentation. Her work has been recognized nationally: she directed Cooking with Kathryn, which won Best Physical Comedy at the FRIGID Fringe Festival and People’s Choice at PORTFringe. She also created the clown show Miss Route 1 for the Boston Fringe and founded the Boston Fringe Festival itself, building a platform for boundary-pushing performance. In addition to her original work, Deby has assistant directed Off-Broadway and continues to champion emerging artists while developing her own inventive projects that challenge and delight audiences. www.debyx.com @debyxiadani on insta

title: Commedia Dell’Arte: The Mastery of Mask & Physical Comedy with Mycah Hogan
description: Commedia Dell’Arte: The Mastery of Mask & Physical Comedy with Mycah Hogan Step into the vibrant, high-stakes, and highly stupid world of Commedia dell’Arte in this immersive two-day intensive. Designed for actors, educators, and anyone who’s mask-curious, thiis workshop aims to strip away the “polite” performer to reveal the raw, hilarious, and wildly human archetypes that have fueled comedy for centuries. Participants will explore the rigorous physicality and spontaneous play required to bring the iconic stock characters—Arlecchino, Capitano, Pantalone, Dottore, and others — to life. Through mask work, ensemble devising, and the study of lazzi (classic comedic business), you’ll learn how to activate these characters in your own body and build authentic (and sometimes surprising) connections to the audience. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your comedic timing, expand your physical range, or simply reclaim a sense of wonder in your craft, this weekend is about unlocking the power of the mask. title: A Moment To Spare
description: A Moment To Spare A Moment to Spare is an interactive comedy show telling a story about a fool (me, Colin) arriving at an existential crossroads after the death of his father (How cliché, I know right?). He and the audience wind up getting sucked into the video game of his life where the objective is simple – rewrite the past so he can be “perfect” in the future. Oh, and just a heads up – he will need your help. If all goes well, this could fix him and probably change the world as we know it. It’s part clown show, part stand-up, and part narrative storytelling where the audience gets a say in how the story gets told. Bio: Colin is a comedian and writer who’s performed in theaters all over the country. He is a member of The Clown School Company and is currently performing as a part of this year’s Hollywood Fringe Festival. He has studied/performed at UCB, The Groundlings, The Clown School, The Elysian Theater, The Comedy Store, the Hollywood Improv, and many more… Instagram link: https://www.instagram.com/ colincoughlin/ Timeline: DOORS: 6:15 PM SHOW: 7:00 PM Age Limit: This event is All Ages, suggested 16+ ID: Valid ID required for alcohol consumption Limited Late Seating: Due to the architecture of our space, the entrance is next to the stage and it is disruptive to the performer to enter late. title: Thom Tran
description: Thom Tran Thom Tran is a Los Angeles–based comedian, actor, musician, and U.S. Army combat veteran whose stand-up career began after surviving a gunshot wound to the back of the head while deployed to Iraq. Following his medical retirement, Tran relocated to Los Angeles in 2008 and quickly immersed himself in the comedy scene. He went on to found The GIs of Comedy, an internationally touring, all-military veteran stand-up group that has performed for U.S. service members stationed and deployed in combat zones worldwide. The group was featured on Larry Charles’ Dangerous World of Comedy (Netflix) and has appeared on CBS and NBC. As a solo act, Tran tours nationally and internationally, including dates across Europe with longtime collaborator Brad Williams, performing in Denmark, Norway, England, Ireland, and beyond. His material blends sharp observational humor with lived experience, delivered with discipline and timing honed both on stage and in service. Based in Hollywood, Tran is a regular at premier clubs including the World Famous Laugh Factory and the Comedy & Magic Club, in addition to theaters and venues throughout Southern California. On screen, Tran has co-starred on NCIS: Los Angeles and SEAL Team (CBS) and appears in the feature film My Dead Friend Zoe alongside Morgan Freeman, Sonequa Martin-Green, and Ed Harris. title: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara
description: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara If you’re a sketch writer, performer, director or teacher who is interested in process, experimentation and discovery, this workshop is for you! This full day session will operate like a professional sketch rehearsal with a focus on material generation and productive exploration. Through writing, improvisation and on-our-feet exercises, we’ll play with a range of techniques to create material. Participants will leave with new creative tools, and new ways to approach writing, performing and developing sketch. Participants should have some prior experience with sketch comedy. A comfort with improvisation is a plus. Come ready to play and let’s see what we can make together! ABOUT ANDY: Andy Miara is a former director for The Second City in Chicago where he also served as a core writing instructor in the Second City Training Center. He is a former head writer of The Onion News Network and co-creator of The Onion’s sister site, Clickhole.com. Alongside Tim Robinson and Mark Raterman, Miara co-founded the sketch group My Mans. The trio developed pilots for Comedy Central and Adult Swim, and created The Thanksgiving House, an immersive theater show in Los Angeles produced by Funny or Die and IFC. Miara has written on animated comedies including Robot Chicken and SuperMansion, and has developed original projects with NBC, TBS, truTV, and Cartoon Network. Most recently, he co-wrote and directed the scripted audio series Get It To Dutch for iHeart Media, and currently has an animated pilot in development at Fox starring Tim Robinson and Cecily Strong. Miara is an Assistant Professor of Screenwriting at Emerson College. Doors: 9:30 AM Start: 10:00 AM End: 4:00 PM Age Limit: This workshop is 18+ Refund Policy: All sales are final. No Refunds. title: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas
description: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas SHOW DESCRIPTION: It is, and is not the words. It’s the situation. You, your partner(s), and imagination in the moment are the situation…. We will be fooling around with written words, using the Dynamics, the Complicities, the Clown Personas, and the Tension States, as a fruitful path for mining the physical and the fun. Very brief texts of Will Shakespeare & Sam Beckett will be supplied…. And you can bring your own. A monologue, a scene, a poem, a manifesto. It’s all grist, darlin’. ARTIST BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo. Recently, in film, she played two old ladies. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now about the Gardner Museum heist. It’s now streaming on Amazon Prime. Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, Physical Comedy, and Acting as Career. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector. Sheriden has directed professionally for the Shakespeare Festival of Dallas, Mother Jones in Chicago, Company Theatre in Los Angeles, Manhattan Class, and WOW Cafe in New York City. She will be directing The Beauty Queen of Leenane for Theater Uncorked this November at Boston Center for the Arts. Her Tufts bio is: https://tdps.tufts.edu/people/faculty/sheriden-thomas Doors: 10:45 AM Start

title: The Future of Higher Ed (FOHE) Boston Presents: David’s Farewell Spectacular & Search for Boston’s Next Co-Lead
description: The Future of Higher Ed (FOHE) Boston Presents: David’s Farewell Spectacular & Search for Boston’s Next Co-Lead EVENT DESCRIPTION: After helping build FOHE Boston into one of the most vibrant higher education and EdTech communities in the country, David is stepping down as Co-Lead. Join us for an evening of celebration, storytelling, questionable decision-making, and the search for his successor. The first half of the evening will feature a farewell tribute to David, reflecting on the events, conversations, and community that have defined FOHE Boston. The second half will feature live “auditions” from aspiring future co-leads, each making their case for why they should help shape the next chapter of the community. Candidates will have 5 minutes to pitch their vision for FOHE Boston. Slides, props, visual aids, costumes, and interpretive dance are not required, but are strongly encouraged. Whether you’re a founder, university leader, investor, operator, student, educator, or simply curious about the future of learning and work, come celebrate the community and help us imagine what’s next. HOST BIO: Future of Higher Education (FOHE) is an essential global community for founders and practitioners focused on the future of postsecondary education and training. With more than 6,000 members worldwide and 600+ in the Boston area, FOHE creates opportunities for meaningful connection, collaboration, and conversation across higher education, workforce development, and educational technology. title: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora
description: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora Step into a world where rebellion meets rhinestones, and fabric tells a story far deeper than fashion. Denim & Desire is a burlesque experience that peels back the seams of history, celebrating denim not just as an icon of style, but as a symbol woven through Black resilience, labor, culture, and expression. From its roots as durable workwear worn by enslaved and working class Black laborers, to its transformation into a global statement of cool shaped by Black musicians, dancers, and tastemakers, denim has always carried more than meets the eye. August 16th, we honor that legacy, thread by thread, strip by strip. Expect a dazzling lineup of performers who will reimagine denim in all its forms, raw, rugged, glamorous, and subversive. Through tease, storytelling, and unapologetic sensuality, each act pays tribute to the Black bodies and voices that turned denim into a canvas of identity and power. This is more than a show. It is a reclamation. A celebration. A strut through history in your best blues. So grab your seats, hold onto your hems, and get ready to witness denim like you have never seen it before. Denim is in our genes. From our enslaved ancestors dressed in negro cloth, to the denim clad cowboys on dude ranches, to denim being reclaimed and made into a statement of rebellion in the civil rights movement, to the repositioning of denim in the world of fashion due in part to black taste makers. On August 16th at The Rockwell, join Bubble Burlesque and an Iconic all black cast to find out how we continue to set your tongue. description: “Be Good” with Paulette OH LOOK! HERE COMES THE MILDEST MAN IMAGINABLE. Paulette stumbles into a room full of the most strangers he’s ever seen, and he doesn’t know whether to panic or mingle—so he does both, for 60 minutes. Sporting a brown sweater and a hot-off-the-fist black eye, he dares to address the room armed with nothing but an arsenal of pleasantries and a monumental fear of rejection. Hot off of a high octane tour of Europe, the UK, and even the east coast of America, certified clown Daniel Maseda brings well-mannered idiot Paulette back to The Rockwell for the very second time with this fan-favorite show that never plays out the same way twice. A perfect evening for anyone who wants to scream at a polite person. As we learn together, we’ll work on a simple sewing project—a drawstring bag—which most students will be able to complete by the end of the class. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: Jerry Bergonzi, Tenor Saxophone A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

title: The Fringe
description: The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone, bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood. Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. George Garzone, Tenor Saxophone Lineup subject to change without notice

title: Bevan Manson Trio ft. Allan Chase
description: $20 at the door / $15 advance / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated 35 years after the release of their underground hit "Rhythm Chowder", pianist/composer Bevan Manson, drummer Matt Wilson and bassist Bob Nieske reunite to play their unique, unpredictable and deeply felt renditions of jazz standards and originals. Saxophonist Allan Chase joins as special guest on a night that marks a full circle moment in Boston jazz history. Here’s a link to their recording “Rhythm Chowder” Bevan Manson has received composing commissions from Sierra Chamber Music, Pacific Philharmonic Foundation, the San Francisco Symphony, clarinetist Gary Gray, the Channel Islands Chamber Orchestra and LACO violist Victoria Miskolczy amongst others. Recently an arranger for Manhattan Transfer vocalist Cheryl Bentyne’s Sondheim album, Mr. Manson has also arranged music for Village Vanguard Orchestra saxophonist Gary Smulyan and L.A. vocalist Cathy Segal Garcia. ​Currently a free-lance composer/arranger and jazz pianist in L.A. and points west, he has been a faculty member at New England Conservatory, Director of UC Jazz at UC Berkeley and jazz faculty at Ventura College. He has also worked in the L.A. film and TV industries. Bevan’s classical works have been recorded on Albany Records; he has a recent jazz release of his on Meistero Music ’The Jazz Cave’. Other recordings have been released on Iris Records and Challenge (Netherlands). Matt Wilson has released thirteen albums as a leader, appeared on morethan 400 others as a sideman and has played with an impressive array of some of the most legendary names in jazz, including Wynton Marsalis, Lee Konitz, Joe Lovano, Pat Metheny, Dewey Redman, Charlie Haden, John Scofield, Joanne Brackeen and Herbie Hancock, just to name a few. title: Gill Aharon Trio
description: Inspired by the cartoon music of the 50s and 60s, the drive of Led Zeppelin, the genius and humor of Frank Zappa, the perfection of Bach, the relentlessness of Ligeti, the courage of Medeski, Martin and Wood, the jam of Phish live, the beauty of the Beatles and the immersive nature of music, I am in pursuit of truth through music. “Sometimes I think of us musicians as kids playing in order to learn how to be adults, but we can just keep playing. I never want my friends and bandmates to feel obliged to do anything. - Gill Aharon

title: Sophie Wellington Album Release + Square Dance!
description: $20 admission / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / seated & standing Celebrate the release of Sophie's new album, Her Bright Smile Haunts Me Still with a intimate and guitar forward solo set, followed by a celebratory square dance! Her Bright Smile Haunts Me Still is Sophie's second album, and it focuses on how to approach playing guitar like a fiddler, singer, and percussive dancer. She uses alternate guitar tunings and "fiddle picking" techniques to emulate the feel and sound of the fiddle. She accompanies her voice using harmonic gravity, rhythmic velocity, and her experience as a ballad singer and jazz vocalist. HBSHMS is artfully recorded, mixed, and produced by Grammy Award winning artist Cathy Fink. Live tracked and performed solo, it is a souvenir of Sophie's dynamic musicianship. Sophie Wellington is an old time fiddler, flatpick guitarist, percussive dancer and jazz vocalist based in Boston, MA. Sophie grew up in Staunton, VA and was raised in its vibrant music community by musician and dance caller Bill Wellington and classical pianist Lynne Mackey. Sophie graduated from Berklee College of Music in 2022 with a degree in jazz voice and American roots music, and has since taught fiddle, flatfooting, guitar, and music theory at numerous festivals and camps. Sophie also toured extensively with musician and modern day bard Willi Carlisle.

title: h2 Live @ The Lilypad
description: $10 cover / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated & standing h2, the fusion project of violinist and composer Luke Norman, plays original compositions and arrangements from their debut EP, “Running Late”. The performance features Luke Norman on violin, Angelo Della Valle on guitar, Anderson Mirafzali on bass, and Nick White on drums. h2 is a Boston-based fusion artist whose music bridges the worlds of jazz, electronic, and experimental rock. His music combines intricate melodies with high-octane grooves that exemplify precision, depth, and a forward-thinking approach to fusion. Drawing inspiration from Mahavishnu Orchestra, Ghost Note, and Machine Girl, his music bridges the analog warmth of classic fusion with the freneticism of contemporary electronic music.

description: Drummer Luther Gray, though largely self-taught, his musical training involved drum lessons from Kim Martin, Larry Bright, Steve Bagby, and Mickey Newman. In 1995 he graduated the University of Miami with a Bachelor of Music, after which he taught privately and performed in the Washington , D.C. area with, among others, Butch Warren, Cecil Payne, Webster Young, Tsunami, Liquorice, Peter Edelman, Jenny Toomey, Bob Butta, and Buck Hill. Since moving to Boston he has resumed teaching private drum lessons and has played with Joe Morris, Jay Hoggard, Joe McPhee, Timo Shanko, Cameron Brown, Allan Chase, Joseph Daley, Sabir Mateen, Roy Campbell, Ida, Geoff Farina, Andrew White, Rob Brown, Bill Lowe, Greg Abate, Raqib Hassan, Bill Pierce, Mitch Seidman, Steve Swell, Joe Beck, Fred Anderson, Ken Vandermark and many others. In addition to his performing schedule Luther teaches art and music at an after-school program for elementary school children.

title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: Jerry Bergonzi, Tenor Saxophone A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

title: The Fringe
description: The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone, bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood. Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. George Garzone, Tenor Saxophone Lineup subject to change without notice

title: Deadword Theatre Co. Presents: naked SARA (no nudity) by Sara Eakman
description: $15 admission / 10:30 doors / 11pm start / seated & standing Some Saras are naked, other Sarahs are clothed. Which one am I? You’ll have to come and see! I have a LOT I want to talk about, and I’ll bet you’ll enjoy what I have to say. Topics discussed will be SEX! GAY! AUTISM! RELIGION! FAMILY! Or as I always say: SGARF! Be prepared to chat with me, because I want to hear all about you! (50% of proceeds will be donated to the Allston Planned Parenthood). Deadword Theatre Co. is a local collection of performers, artists, and friends looking to expand the Boston arts community. We specialize in new takes on classic works with an emphasis on hiring student, non-union, and amateur artists. Sara Eakman is a frequent collaborator of Deadword, most recently appearing as Anne in Home Life and Casca in Julius Caesar. This is her first original show. Instagram links: @deadwordtheatre, @saraeakman, @charlielunardi

title: Jesse Gallagher + Steve Fell
description: Jesse Gallagher began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman st. At the time Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine. The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts Wu-Tang Clan, Toots & The Maytals, The Flaming Lips & Dr. Dog. Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/ Sam Cohen, Willy Mason, Lilys, Nick Nicely, Doug Tuttle & Edan. Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. Steve Fell is a guitarist, composer, and educator whose performing and recording career over the last twenty five years has reached across the boundaries of jazz, experimental, funk, free form improvisation, rock, electronic, reggae/calypso, hip-hop, psych, and many others. He co-leads the groups Clear Audience, Quantum Banditos, Dome Room, and Astronomico, leads a trio under his own name, and collaborates with numerous bands and artists.

title: Gill Aharon Trio
description: Inspired by the cartoon music of the 50s and 60s, the drive of Led Zeppelin, the genius and humor of Frank Zappa, the perfection of Bach, the relentlessness of Ligeti, the courage of Medeski, Martin and Wood, the jam of Phish live, the beauty of the Beatles and the immersive nature of music, I am in pursuit of truth through music. “Sometimes I think of us musicians as kids playing in order to learn how to be adults, but we can just keep playing. The game of playing music together is too much fun to make it work. With that in mind, I refuse to write arrangements. I never want my friends and bandmates to feel obliged to do anything. - Gill Aharon

title: Pixel Party
description: Build a wooden model of an iconic Nintendo character! Each participant will be given a set of painted wooden blocks that correspond with their chosen character. You will then be guided step by step on how to glue the blocks together to make a wooden model of a character from the 8-bit era of gaming. All materials will be provided and no experience is necessary. Final sculptures will vary in size. The tallest is Samus (13 inches) and the shortest are Mario & Link (each 6.7 inches). If you do not finish your sculpture during the event, you are welcome to take everything you need to finish it at home. If you would like to build a character that is not listed in the dropdown menu, feel free to email robertpatricklynch@gmail.com with requests. This is an all ages event. Children under 13 should be signed up at their parent/guardian's discretion. They will need adult supervision and have the ability to sit and do a project for 1-2 hours without being disruptive.

title: Get to the Gig Presents Widowspeak with Neu Blume
description: Widowspeak is a band that riffs on big emotions without being too self-serious. The sweetness, even silliness, of an extended limerent phase that becomes as all-consuming as a pulpy trade paperback. Cars and their drivers serve as a way to talk aboutcodependency. And old love gets worn in, soft as an old t-shirt. If music can simultaneously be naturalistic and noir, saturated and lush, that is Widowspeak. They’re a band that knows how to set a scene. We bring the good vibes, you just bring yourselves. Snacks and drinks available all show. At Nebula Night, everyone becomes a star! General Admission is $10 per ticket. title: Somerville Fermentation Festival
description: A celebration of food and culture in Somerville, MA Join us for the second year of the Somerville Fermentation Festival, an annual celebration of the world of fermented foods and the layers of community that create them! Sample & take home a diverse range of fermented foods & beverages, learn how to make your own sauerkraut, swap starter cultures with other local fermenters, and attend presentations by experts in the field.

title: Bill Blumenreich Presents: Chill Towards Enlightenment: A Stoke Seminar with Chad Goes Deep
description: A satirical ted talk seminar on his stoke philosophy where he tackles the question: “Why is bummer so prevalent in our society and how do we transcend it?” Join us on this beautiful journey and learn Chad’s transformative technique, The Chill Method, which will help you reclaim your inner joy and set you on a new path to enjoy this radical adventure we call life.

title: Sam Bondi and Holly Sverdrup Hoyer Exhibition Opening Reception
description: Holly Megan Sverdrup Hoyer (hmsh) is a watercolor artist based in Central Mass. A graduate of Emerson College’s Theatrical Design and Production program, she has transitioned her training as a set designer into the creation of whimsical illustrations. While she often draws inspiration from nature, she takes a special joy in creating pieces inspired by language – such as a quote, a typo, a conversation, or a song. Holly loves to find and render the simple beauty in the small things we come across in life. She is very interested in history, and is a member of the Daughters of the American Revolution. When she’s not in her studio, she can often be found crocheting, camping, reading, or spending time with her spouse and their two chaotic cats. She gets equally excited about a new brush as she does a nice spreadsheet. Samuel D. Bondi is a multi-media artist who specializes in soft pastels and acrylic. He is a graduate of Emerson College’s Theater Education program and a bartender by trade. An education inimprovisation and playmaking encouraged him to explore the abstract in his art. Experiencing the process of layering color and pattern to create is often prioritized over the planning of an imagined final product.

title: Smut Slam
description: What’s a SMUT SLAM? I’m so glad you asked! It’s a fast-paced storytelling open mic based on REAL life, REAL lust, REAL sex. Consenting Slammers sign up on the night of to tell a 5-minute dirty story, based on their real lives, and a lucky 8-10 names will be drawn at random. A panel of celebrity judges will be on hand to evaluate your stories, and bestow the top three Slammers with a sack of sexy swag from Good Vibrations Harvard Square . You will also have the opportunity to win goodies from NJOY by submitting your anonymous questions and confessions! RULES: No notes! This is storytelling. No costumes or props! This is not theatre. Only 5 minutes! (With a 1 minute grace period) The story must be real and have happened to YOU. Stories are often funny and/or epic win but we want to encourage people to consider sharing their sad, disturbing, poignant, serious, simple and/or ‘fail’ experiences too. TAKE NOTE: Smut Slam is queer-friendly, kink-friendly AND vanilla-friendly, fat-friendly, poly-friendly… Yes, we are very friendly. We welcome people with all types and amounts of sexual experiences to our space. We DO NOT welcome stories involving racism, transphobia, homophobia, sexism or any form of discrimination, fetishization or objectification. Also, CONSENT IS KEY.
